governance.attested_by: neiso-38 merrimack-availability 2026-06-28 (supersedes neiso-37 weather-floor; new NEISO keeper candidate)
governance.note: neiso-38 = the neiso-37 keeper recipe (measured Algonquin/EIA-MA-citygate DAILY gas-hub basis overlay + dual-fuel oil re-attribution + EIA-930-pinned hydro budget with 2024 plant-capacity backfill + biomass/OTHER measured must-run + historic CAMPD outage overlay + storage vintage ramp + the dual-limb temperature-correlated reliability floor neiso_temp_reliability_floor) WITH ONE correctness fix: neiso_floor_outage_exempt (default ON). ROOT CAUSE (CLAUDE.md #11): the CAMPD unit-outage overlay was ZEROING the lone Merrimack-class COAL unit (Plant_Code 2364) and the lone ST_GAS unit, so the temperature floor's frac x available bound -- and any economic dispatch -- was structurally capped at ~0 and no downstream lever (floor, daily-basis economics, or the gas-coldsnap derate) could ever recover the coal/steam energy. Two compounding bugs in the overlay, both specific to a winter cold-snap peaker: (1) the unit-outage detector defines an outage as a sustained CF < 5% gap >= 2 days -- a rule built for BASELOAD coal/CC -- so for a unit that runs only on cold snaps (sub-10% annual CF) it misreads the unit's ECONOMIC IDLENESS as a forced outage and books nearly the whole year as outaged; (2) the derate fraction unit_capacity_mw / plant_capacity_mw is taken against the 108 MW model bin while the CSV's unit capacities are the real ~460 MW Merrimack plant (units 1+2 = 113.6 + 345.6 MW), so a SINGLE coal-unit 'outage' over-derates the 108 MW bin past full and clips availability to zero. Net effect measured directly: Merrimack COAL availability was 0 of 8760 h in 2024 (a unit that actually generated 0.24 TWh), 3% of hours in 2023, 22% in 2025. The fix EXEMPTS the two floor classes (COAL, ST_GAS) from the unit-outage overlay when neiso_temp_reliability_floor governs them -- exactly as ct_mustrun_per_plant exempts its reliability-floor units from the WEFOR/planned-outage derate -- because the floor's commitment fraction is regressed from each unit's OWN measured CAMPD capacity factor, a regression that already nets out the unit's real maintenance downtime; re-applying the CF-gap overlay on top double-counts it. This is a correctness fix, NOT a fit: the exemption is binary (overlay on/off for the floor classes), its magnitude is governed entirely by the floor's UNCHANGED measured-CF coefficients, nothing is tuned to a coal or price residual, and the model still UNDER-runs coal after the fix (it is not pinned to the actual). ATTRIBUTION (apples-to-apples on identical current-main code, neiso_39_nofix_control_3yr = same recipe with --no-neiso-floor-outage-exempt): coal grid-delivered 0.006/0.000/0.043 -> 0.058/0.113/0.234 TWh (the 2024 control of exactly 0.000 is the availability bug made visible), ST_GAS likewise recovers; gas family 53.4/57.9/60.7 (essentially unchanged from control, in-band C2), CC_REGULAR slightly LOWER (helps the C1 item), system mean LMP 34.6/39.1/68.3 (unchanged), CO2 +0.02/+0.06/+0.11 Mt (<0.5%). So the fix is a Pareto improvement: it recovers the coal/steam reliability energy a definite overlay bug had erased, while every PASS criterion is held or improved. SEPARATELY TESTED AND REJECTED this session: the temperature-dependent winter gas-availability derate (neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate) -- a candidate structural lever for the residual broad-winter coal -- is BYTE-IDENTICAL to this keeper on coal/gas/price across all three years (neiso_probe_coldsnap_derate). It fires (72/144/304 cold-window hours, frac up to the 0.20 cap) but removes too little gas to lift the clearing price or pull more coal in: NEISO is not capacity- or reserve-short even on cold snaps -- the ~6.8 GW dual-fuel fleet stays available on oil -- so the derate (and the RCPF reserve co-opt) do not bind in the backcast, confirming neiso-37's finding. The derate stays default-OFF (it was never enabled in this keeper). IMPACT (this keeper): gas family model 53.39/57.89/60.67 vs EIA-930 grid 52.75/56.91/59.76 (+1.2%/+1.7%/+1.5%, C2 PASS all years); system mean LMP 34.62/39.10/68.29 vs RT actual 35.70/39.50/65.89 (-3.0%/-1.0%/+3.6%, C3a PASS); CO2 -0.5%/-0.3%/+3.3% vs eGRID (C5a PASS -- 2025 +3.3% is marginally above neiso-37's +2.4% because the recovered coal adds ~0.1 Mt, still well within band); C3b price-shape PASS; C4 dispatch correlation PASS. No offer/adder/pin/haircut was added or tuned to a residual. The model is not pinned to either actual.

The no-fix control bundle neiso_39_nofix_control_3yr and the rejected derate probe neiso_probe_coldsnap_derate were solved on the same current-main code for attribution. exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (gas-vs-EIA-930-OTHER fold-in categorization, not a model miss)
exceptions.reason: The gas FAMILY is within tolerance (C2 PASS, +1.2%); the per-class C1 gate flags CC_REGULAR because the small family-level surplus concentrates in the marginal combined-cycle unit AND the per-class actual is deflated by the geothermal+biomass that NEISO folds into the EIA-930 'Natural Gas' cell (reconcile_vintage_classes subtracts ~1.6 TWh of NG-cell-folded non-gas from the gas target). The model books that OTHER/biomass residual (process gas / landfill / purchased steam) as its own measured must-run rows and serves the un-foldable remainder with marginal CC, so ~1 TWh of the gas the grid attributes to NG-cell-folded non-gas sources lands on CC_REGULAR. This is the same EIA-923-vs-EIA-930 OTHER categorization difference neiso-37 documents, unchanged by the availability fix (the fix slightly LOWERS CC_REGULAR by displacing a little marginal gas with the recovered coal). Closable only by reconciling the OTHER/NG-fold-in categorization on both sides, NEVER by injecting the residual or scaling CC to the deflated benchmark (fitting). Carried HARD caveat.

exceptions.metric: C1 coal + steam-gas grid-delivered energy under-run (winter reliability/fuel-security runner)
exceptions.magnitude: COAL_BIT model 0.058/0.113/0.234 vs actual 0.181/0.238/0.271 TWh (2023/24/25); ST_GAS model 0.051/0.021/0.029 vs 0.206/0.107/0.304 TWh. Each per-class miss (-0.12/-0.12/-0.04 coal) is WITHIN the C1 per-class absolute band (+/-~0.96-1.04 TWh) so it does NOT trip the C1 gate, but it is a real, persistent structural under-run -- previously undocumented and largely masked by the availability bug.
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (structural; same winter fuel-inventory / reliability-commitment family as the C3c price-tail and C5b storage items)
exceptions.reason: NEW caveat, surfaced by the availability fix. The fix removed a definite overlay bug that had erased the energy (control coal 0.006/0.000/0.043 -> 0.058/0.113/0.234), but a residual under-run remains, largest in the LOW-gas years 2023/2024. Mechanism: the energy-only LP runs Merrimack and the lone steam unit only at the temperature-floor commitment plus the few hours delivered gas is dear enough to put coal (HR 11.337 x coal fuel ~ $30-45/MWh) genuinely in merit; in 2023/24 Henry Hub was $2.5/$2.2 and gas-CC out-competed coal most of the winter, so the LP holds coal near the floor. The REAL units ran more -- a winter fuel-security / local-reliability commitment (oil/coal/steam held online against multi-day cold-snap gas-deliverability risk) that a cost-based merit order cannot see, the SAME unobserved winter-scarcity driver behind the C3c >$300 tail and the C5b storage spread. The candidate forward-faithful lever (neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate) was tested this session and does NOT close it (byte-identical: NEISO is not reserve-short, the dual-fuel oil fleet keeps the cold-window price at oil parity, so removing a small gas slice neither lifts price nor pulls in coal). Closable only by the documented future build that makes the winter oil/coal reliability commitment forward-reproducible (e.g. a fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability constraint whose shadow price lands on the tightest cold hours and is condition-responsive), NEVER by cranking the floor slope/cap (regressed from measured CF, must not be tuned to a TWh residual) or by an offer adder. The 108 MW model bin for Merrimack (vs the real ~460 MW plant) also bounds the maximum recoverable coal and is a separate fleet-representation item noted for follow-up.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent / reserve scarcity, capped here by the dual-fuel oil-parity)
exceptions.reason: The model pins every top-price hour at the flat dual-fuel oil-parity cap (~$258/MWh): when delivered gas spikes on a cold day, dual-fuel units switch to oil (apply_dual_fuel_pricing) and the marginal price cannot exceed oil parity, so the energy-only LP produces 0 hours > $300. Two faithful ISO-NE scarcity structures (in-LP operating-reserve co-optimization on the published NEISO RCPF requirements; the temperature-dependent winter gas-availability derate inject_neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate) were re-confirmed this session NOT to bind in 2023-25: NEISO is not operating-reserve-short -- the ~6.8 GW dual-fuel fleet stays available on oil and imports/hydro/storage/floored-steam keep reserve headroom above the 1,800/1,200 MW requirements even with a 20% cold-window gas derate (reserve_price stays 0). Both are kept as default-off infrastructure that binds in tighter forecast years. The real residual driver is winter fuel-INVENTORY scarcity rent (oil/peaker units rationing limited on-site distillate over a multi-day cold snap); distillate is a global liquid fuel whose commodity price does not spike like pipeline gas basis, so a cold-day oil adder would be a forbidden residual fit. The only forward-faithful fix is modeling the oil fleet as inventory-limited (a seasonal oil-burn budget like hydro, whose shadow price IS the scarcity rent) -- a documented future build, not closable by an adder/offer tune. Accepted caveat.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (downstream of the price_tail / reserve-scarcity item)
exceptions.reason: Storage arbitrage throughput tracks the peak-to-trough price spread, which is compressed because the LP caps the cold-hour tail at the dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258, 0 hours > $300; see the price_tail caveat). The reserve co-optimization and gas-availability derate do not widen the spread in the backcast (NEISO is not reserve-short, reserve_price=0), and the Merrimack availability fix does not touch the price spread, so this is NOT a storage-model error: it closes only when the winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent is recovered via the forward-faithful oil-burn-budget constraint, never via a storage or offer tune.
